releases.title: GPT-5.6 Sol price cut — $5/$30 → $4/$20 per 1M
releases.summary: OpenAI cut Sol's API price by 'over 20%' ($5 → $4 input, $30 → $20 output per 1M tokens), promotional through at least Nov 21, 2026. Subscription usage unaffected.
releases.why: If Sol is your top-tier pick, re-run your cost-per-task maths — every effort ladder on this page that plots Sol uses the old price.

releases.title: Google releases Gemini 3.7 Flash
releases.summary: An algorithmic update three weeks after 3.6 Flash, billed as Google's 'most intelligent workhorse model yet' for coding, web dev and agents. Introductory price $0.75/$3.75 per 1M through Dec 31, 2026, then $1.50/$7.50. Stated gains over 3.6 Flash: FrontierCode 1.1 43.6% (from 34.4%), DeepSWE v1.1 65.3% (from 49.0%).
releases.why: The cheap-and-capable tier moved: at $0.75/$3.75 this is the price of a small model with mid-tier coding scores. The intro price doubles on Jan 1 — budget for that.

releases.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro goes GA as '0813' — and gets peak-hour pricing
releases.summary: V4 Pro leaves preview (1M context, 384K max output). Pricing now splits peak vs off-peak: output $1.98/1M off-peak vs $3.96 peak; cache-miss input $0.66 vs $1.32. Peak hours 01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Mon–Fri, effective Aug 16.
releases.why: Overnight bulk jobs just got a clock: schedule them off-peak or pay double. The flat 'cheapest frontier-ish coder' story now depends on when you run.

releases.title: xAI releases Grok 4.6
releases.summary: Frontier multimodal model built on Grok 4.5, aimed at long-running agents, coding and visual work. 500K context; $2/$6 per 1M under 200K prompt tokens, $4/$12 above; four effort levels (low → xhigh). No benchmark numbers on xAI's own page.
releases.why: On CursorBench it tops the board at a fraction of Opus-tier cost (see the effort ladders). Watch the 200K-token price cliff on long contexts.

releases.title: GPT-5.6 Luna −80%, Terra −20%
releases.summary: Luna drops from $1/$6 to $0.20/$1.20 per 1M; Terra from $2.50/$15 to $2/$12. Sol unchanged at the time (cut separately on Aug 21).
releases.why: Luna at $0.20/$1.20 is now a bulk-work candidate, not just a chat tier. Any ladder or chart costed before Jul 30 overstates Luna by 5x.

releases.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5
releases.summary: Opus-tier pricing ($5/$25 per M, same as Opus 4.8) with Fable-class coding: 43.3% on Anthropic's Frontier-Bench v0.1 agentic-coding run vs Fable 5's 33.7% and Opus 4.8's 18.7%, and within 0.5% of Fable 5's peak CursorBench 3.2 score at max effort — at roughly half Fable's cost per task. 1M context, 128K output, five effort levels (low → max). Per-benchmark public numbers (SWE-bench Verified, GPQA) not published yet.
releases.why: If you pay for Claude: this is the new default for hard coding and agent work — Fable-level results at half the price. If you were paying Fable's $10/$50 for coding, check whether Opus 5 covers it.

releases.title: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3
releases.summary: 2.8T-param open-weight MoE (largest to date) at $3/$15 per M, 1M context, native vision. Tops the Frontend Code Arena (1679 Elo) ahead of Claude Fable 5, winning 6 of 7 frontend categories. Full weights due ~July 27; SWE-bench Verified not yet published.
releases.why: If you build front-end or web UI: the new top pick for frontend coding — it edges out even Fable 5 in blind tests, at a fraction of the price ($3/$15).

releases.title: GPT-5.6 (Sol/Terra/Luna) reaches general availability
releases.summary: Three-tier family (Sol $5/$30, Terra $2.50/$15, Luna $1/$6) tops the Artificial Analysis Coding Index; previewed June 26 behind a US-government access list.
releases.why: If you're on ChatGPT/OpenAI: three tiers now — Sol (top), Terra (value, ~$2.50/$15), Luna (cheap). Terra is the sweet spot for most.

releases.title: xAI releases Grok 4.5
releases.summary: 'Opus-class' token-efficient coding/agentic model at $2/$6 per M — far cheaper than Opus 4.8 — bundled into Cursor; not available in EU at launch.
releases.why: If you use Grok: the first version genuinely competitive for coding (86/100) at a low $2/$6.

releases.title: Anthropic redeploys Claude Fable 5
releases.summary: Fable 5 came back online after the US government lifted a June 12 export-control order that had pulled it offline — an AI-governance flashpoint.
releases.why: Only matters for the hardest agent/reasoning runs — it's premium ($10/$50) and access-restricted; most people are better served by Opus or Sonnet.

releases.title: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5
releases.summary: Cheaper agent-focused model, near-Opus quality; intro pricing $2/$10 per M through Aug 31 (then $3/$15), 1M context, default on Free/Pro.

benchmarks_legend.swe_bench: SWE-bench Verified — % of real-world GitHub issues resolved end-to-end (agentic coding). Note: several 2026 models published only SWE-bench Pro, a different/harder variant, so their Verified cell is null.
benchmarks_legend.gpqa: GPQA Diamond — % correct on graduate-level, Google-proof science reasoning questions. Figures sourced from Epoch AI are independently run and reported at the reasoning-effort setting Epoch used (max for Opus 5, Kimi K3, GPT-5.6 Terra and Luna; xhigh for Sonnet 5; high for Grok 4.5), so they are best-case settings rather than defaults.
benchmarks_legend.aime: AIME — % on advanced high-school competition math (American Invitational Mathematics Examination).
benchmarks_legend.mmlu_pro: MMLU-Pro — % on a harder, multi-discipline knowledge and reasoning benchmark.

notes: Pricing is verified against official vendor pricing pages (standard tier, USD per 1M tokens) — treat it as the reliable layer. Benchmarks are directional: they mix primary leaderboards, Epoch AI's independently-run figures, and third-party aggregators, and a confidence flag rides on every model. Claude Opus 5 (released 2026-07-23) is priced at Anthropic's published $5/$25; its GPQA (93.9) is Epoch's independent run, but SWE-bench Verified is still unpublished, so its coding score remains an agentic-suite-led estimate at medium confidence. Kimi K3 is scored on its frontend-coding lead (#1 in the Frontend Code Arena); its GPQA (93.1) is Epoch-run, SWE-bench Verified is still unpublished, and its open-weight release (slated 2026-07-27) has not been re-verified as shipped here — treat self-hosting as unconfirmed. Several 2026 models publish only agentic evals that don't map to SWE-bench Verified; those cells are left blank rather than cross-filed. A blank (—) means 'not reliably sourced,' never a guess. Sonnet 5 shows its current intro price ($2/$10; rises to $3/$15 on Sept 1, 2026). Re-verify any single benchmark against a primary leaderboard before betting real spend on it.

usage.basis: No single "most used" exists — each lens measures a different population and ranks models differently. Figures are ~June–July 2026 and lag a couple of weeks, so the newest models (GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, Sonnet 5) aren't ranked yet.

lenses.label: Developers
lenses.note: Cheap open-weight models win on raw volume; Anthropic & OpenAI win on dollars spent. Chinese labs are ~44–52% of all tokens.

lenses.label: Consumers
lenses.note: Consumer web visits only (undercounts mobile & embedded) — a totally different crowd from the API developers.

coding_score_note: Coding score (0–100) is a unified, comparable coding-ability estimate. Where an official SWE-bench Verified % exists it IS that number (high confidence). Where it doesn't — several strong 2026 models ship before formal benchmarks — it's estimated from sourced signals (Artificial Analysis Coding Index, LMArena Code Elo, SWE-bench Pro, LiveCodeBench) calibrated against the benchmarked models (medium confidence), or expert consensus (low). Each row shows its basis and confidence. These signals sometimes disagree — treat medium/low scores as directional.
use_well_note: use_well = practical, plain-English guidance on getting the most from a model you already have. Derived from the model's sourced pricing, context, cache and mode facts above (plus vendor-documented features like Claude's adaptive thinking) — guidance, not benchmarks. Same independence rule: factual, cost-first, never promotional.

effort_ladders.method: Values digitised from the published figure in Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 announcement — point positions read off the chart, so treat costs as ±~5% and scores as ±~0.5 points. The max-effort endpoints are exact: 43.3 / 33.7 / 18.7 are quoted numerically in the launch coverage and match the plotted points, which is what anchors the rest of the reading.
effort_ladders.harness: Internal run of Frontier-Bench v0.1 on the mini-SWE-agent harness with a GKE backend; mean reward over 5 attempts per task. Opus 4.8 served as fallback on safety-classifier refusals for Opus 5 and Fable 5.
effort_ladders.caveat: Anthropic's own benchmark, own harness, own run — and three of the four models plotted are its own. Read it for the SHAPE of each model's cost/quality curve (where extra spend stops buying accuracy), not as a settled cross-lab ranking. No third party has reproduced it.

series.label: GPT-5.6 Sol
series.level_note: OpenAI exposes its own reasoning-effort settings, not Anthropic's five names — these are the rungs as Anthropic plotted them, so the labels are positional rather than an exact setting-for-setting match.

effort_ladders.method: Exact published values, not digitised from a picture: taken from Epoch AI's CC-BY benchmark data export (cursorbench_external.csv in benchmark_data.zip, file dated 2026-08-23), which mirrors Cursor's own CursorBench 3.2 leaderboard (Cursor's changelog: Aug 11 2026 'Updated Sonnet 5 results to account for adjusted pricing'). Score is the published fraction correct as a percentage; cost is Cursor's per-task figure from the tokens each model actually used at its published per-million pricing (input, cache read, cache write, output). Rungs are keyed on the file's 'Reasoning level' column. Five of the most-used models are plotted (Opus 5, Sonnet 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, Grok 4.6, Gemini 3.7 Flash) so the chart stays readable — Fable 5, Opus 4.8, GPT-5.6 Terra, Luna, GPT-5.5, Kimi K3 and others are in the source file; any model-and-rung missing a cost or score is dropped, never interpolated.
effort_ladders.harness: Cursor's agent running CursorBench 3.2 (instruction-following and advanced tool-use problems added Jul 8 2026), one entry per reasoning-effort setting. Cursor notes results are subject to variance and small score differences may not be meaningful.
effort_ladders.caveat: Independent of Anthropic, but not of everyone: CursorBench is run and published by Cursor, which ships its own coding model (Composer), so it is a benchmark by a company with a horse in the coding race. Epoch AI mirrors those numbers under CC-BY, it does not re-run them — and Epoch has its own disclosed conflict elsewhere, having had OpenAI fund the FrontierMath benchmark with dataset access, which it disclosed only after the fact. Read this as a second opinion measured on a different task by a different party, not as a neutral referee settling the question.

effort_ladders.x_label: API cost per task (USD, log scale)
effort_ladders.method: Digitised from the interactive score-vs-cost chart in OpenAI's GPT-5.6 launch post: point positions were pulled from the chart's SVG and calibrated against the six values the page states in its table (Sol 88.8, GPT-5.5 85.6, Fable 5 83.1, Opus 4.8 78.9, Gemini 3.1 Pro 70.7 all reproduce to ±0.1), so treat scores as ±0.3 points and costs as ±$0.03. Effort labels are not in the chart markup; each model's points are ordered by cost and labelled low → max by position, which matches the page's statement that Sol ships with xhigh and max rungs. GPT-5.5 has four points. Models with a single point (Fable 5, Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.1 Pro) are not plotted — one point isn't a ladder.
effort_ladders.harness: OpenAI's own run of Terminal-Bench 2.1. Cost is OpenAI's estimate, not a measurement: the page's footnote says latency and API cost were estimated by looking at production behaviour and simulating offline at regular API pricing, and that real-world results may vary substantially.
effort_ladders.caveat: A lab publishing about its own models, on a chart it drew. Terminal-Bench is an accepted third-party benchmark, but this run, harness and cost model are OpenAI's and have not been reproduced. Two things to know: the page's summary table states Terra 87.4% and Luna 84.7%, higher than the top of their plotted curves (84.3 / 82.5) with no explanation; and OpenAI cut Luna's price 80% and Terra's 20% on Jul 30 and Sol's 20% on Aug 21, so the plotted costs are launch-day prices and now overstate what those rungs cost.
